b1-review-3.R3.1 Back from the south:
Mrs. Lima: Welcome back, Danny! Would you mind taking your boots off at the door? They're filthy!
Danny: Not at all! Sorry, Mrs. Lima. I've just walked from the bus station.
Ana: So, tell us everything! How was Patagonia?
Danny: Absolutely amazing. The glaciers were huge, and the lakes were such a bright blue that they looked fake. Although it was summer, it was freezing at night.
Bruno: Did you wear my belt?
Danny: Every day! And my ugly old green wool sweater. I'd never been so happy to have it.
Ana: And the wind? Paulo told me that the wind there was terrible.
Danny: It was. At first I couldn't walk straight, but I got used to it after a few days.
Bruno: Did you meet anyone interesting?
Danny: Yes! Tomás, who has lived alone by a lake for twenty-five years. He'd worked in an office before he moved there. He told me he would never go back to the city.
Mrs. Lima: A hermit! And how was Buenos Aires?
Danny: Great. The hotel, which was near the center, was small but spotless. There was a mistake on my bill, but I asked politely, and they took it off.
Ana: Did you have any problems with money this time?
Danny: No. I took some cash in case my card didn't work, and I didn't use street ATMs unless I had to.
Bruno: Smart. Did Buenos Aires feel touristy?
Danny: Some places did. However, the locals were really friendly. On the other hand, everything was more expensive than I'd expected.
Mrs. Lima: Well, you're home now. Danny, could you pass me your plate? There's soup.
Danny: Chicken soup? Mrs. Lima, you're the best!
Ana: Oh, and Carol says hi. She told me she had found the perfect dress for Linda's wedding.
